standard_prerequisites.name: The Picard group of a ringed space is the first cohomology group of its sheaf of invertible functions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-h1-invertible (canonical Stacks tag 09NU); invoked at proof lines 626-629
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification of Pic with H^1 of the sheaf of units, which is what turns the long exact sequence of units into the displayed sequence of Picard groups.

core_obligations: Produce the exponential short exact sequence: for a first order thickening X contained in X' with ideal sheaf I, the map sending a local section f of I to the invertible section 1 + f of O_{X'}^* is well defined precisely because I^2 = 0, and it gives the short exact sequence of sheaves of abelian groups 0 -> I -> O_{X'}^* -> O_X^* -> 0 (proof lines 619-625).

Write down the associated long exact cohomology sequence, which begins 0 -> H^0(X, I) -> H^0(X', O_{X'}^*) -> H^0(X, O_X^*) -> H^1(X, I) -> ... and continues with the higher cohomology of I, so that the displayed diagram is that sequence with the H^0 of units and the displayed arrows (proof lines 619-622, cf. the diagram at lines 604-613).

Insert the Picard groups into the sequence: replace the first cohomology of the sheaves of invertible functions by the Picard groups of X' and X using the identification of Pic with H^1 of the units, which turns the tail of the sequence into H^1(X, I) -> Pic(X') -> Pic(X) -> H^2(X, I) -> ... and proves the assertion (proof lines 626-629).
proof_roadmap: Form the exponential map f -> 1 + f from the ideal sheaf I into the units of O_{X'}, using I^2 = 0 to keep the result invertible and to make the map multiplicative (proof lines 619-625).
Recognise the resulting short exact sequence of sheaves of abelian groups and take its long exact cohomology sequence (proof lines 619-622).
Identify the H^1 of the sheaves of units with the Picard groups via the standard cohomological description of Pic, which yields the displayed exact sequence in abelian groups (proof lines 626-629).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts a canonical exact sequence 0 -> H^0(X, I) -> H^0(X', O_{X'}^*) -> H^0(X, O_X^*) -> H^1(X, I) -> Pic(X') -> Pic(X) -> H^2(X, I) for a first order thickening X contained in X' with ideal sheaf I (statement lines 600-615). What has to be seen is that the ideal sheaf, which is only an O_X-module of square-zero square, sits inside the sheaf of units of O_{X'} through the exponential map f -> 1 + f, and that this really is a short exact sequence of sheaves of abelian groups whose long exact cohomology sequence is the displayed one (proof lines 621-625). The final step replaces the H^1 of the units by the Picard groups, which is a standard identification invoked by citation (proof lines 626-629). The claim is H2: one conceptual construction, short and precise.
